summary: Principal Technical Program Manager with over 10 years experience tackling the hardest integrity challenges at Meta.
about: Technical Product Leader with a foundation in Computer Engineering and an MBA. Proven track record at Meta (Facebook) of bridging the gap between complex engineering requirements and high-level business strategy. I specialize in leading cross-functional teams of technical and non-technical stakeholders to deliver business-critical objectives, ranging from public-facing products to sophisticated internal infrastructure.

employerSummary: My career at Meta began with a "boots on the ground" approach to operations. As an Analyst in 2015, I acted as a force multiplier for the team,
shipping code, managing complex vendor relationships, and translating technical requirements for sales and their customers. This role taught me how
to navigate the Meta ecosystem from the inside out. By owning the end-to-end delivery of diverse projects, I transitioned from a generalist

contributor to a dedicated TPM, carrying forward a "whatever it takes" philosophy to project delivery at scale.

As a TPM, each program I took on grew in scope and complexity. What started as owning discrete workstreams evolved into leading multi-team, cross-functional programs with significant regulatory and business stakes. That progression pushed me to grow beyond execution and into leadership, becoming someone teams could rely on to navigate ambiguity, align competing priorities, and deliver under pressure.
highlights: Own Meta's global regulatory reporting program, delivering transparency obligations across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Reality Labs, and all other apps and surfaces. Scaled reporting output by 200% over two years with minimal headcount growth by driving investments in tooling, data hygiene, and automation.

Took over ownership of the [Community Standards Enforcement Report](https://transparency.meta.com/reports/community-standards-enforcement/) and shipped its first meaningful update in years, introducing a new precision metric that publicly tracks enforcement mistakes. Wrote the supporting methodology documentation, aligned cross-functional teams on metric definitions and product experiences required to sustain the metric over time, and delivered on [Mark Zuckerberg's public commitment](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/01/meta-more-speech-fewer-mistakes/) to greater transparency around content moderation accuracy.

Led audit responses to inquiries from the EU Election Commission and the Federal Trade Commission, drawing on improved logging and data organization practices built to meet rising regulatory demands. Responses included detailed technical explanations of how logging systems work, where data challenges arose, and how those challenges were resolved to ensure the accuracy of reported figures. Satisfying these inquiries was critical, as non-compliance or inaccurate reporting carried the risk of formal investigations and significant financial penalties.

Directed a high-stakes compliance initiative in response to civil rights litigation, leading a cross-functional team to build an advertiser certification portal that secured platform integrity while mitigating revenue loss through a strategic phased rollout.

Engineered a scalable enforcement infrastructure for political advertising that neutralized reviewer bias through a novel "label-first" UX, while reducing ad latency by enabling multi-policy parallel processing.

Collaborated with engineering and policy teams to execute Meta’s Financial Services ad policy rollout, integrating ML classifiers and automated enforcement that prevented 1M+ misleading impressions in the first week.

Headed a pilot program to protect legitimate advertiser revenue by identifying approved business models prone to automated misclassification; reduced false-positive rejections by 50% while maintaining a flat prevalence of violating impressions.

employerSummary: My tenure at National Instruments was a masterclass in the two pillars of Technical Program Management:
technical communication and operational scale. Starting as an Applications Engineer, I had to troubleshoot
complex deployments for world-class scientists—often "flying blind" without hardware access. This forced
me to master the art of technical translation: diagnosing invisible problems and adapting my explanations

to match the technical depth of each stakeholder.

Later, as a Software Engineer, I moved from solving individual problems to managing high-volume complexity.
While most groups focused on a single product pipeline, my team developed the driver installers that supported
a dozen different hardware teams simultaneously. Navigating those parallel lifecycles and managing competing
dependencies across dozens of devices was a turning point for me. I realized that while I respected the craft
of coding, my true impact lay in the "big picture"—orchestrating complex technical requirements and aligning
disparate teams to ship at scale.
Long before managing large-scale technical programs, I was at a workbench, taking student and faculty
computers apart to find the 'why' behind a failure. This role was my first lesson in the importance of
systematic isolation—testing known variables to uncover the root cause of a problem. Beyond hardware, I
began looking for operational efficiencies, writing my first scripts to automate the deployment of
public-facing computer labs. It taught me the value of a 'trust but verify' mindset and established the
logical rigor I now use to navigate complex technical dependencies.
